issues.body: `workflow_running_package_tests` applies `_NPM_TEST_RE` and `_selects_workspace` independently to the whole step chunk. This can combine separate commands: for example, a step containing `npm test` at the repository root followed by `npm ci -w @sparq/newpkg` is accepted for `newpkg`, although its `test` script never runs. `_NPM_TEST_RE` is also broad enough to cross command/newline boundaries (for example `npm ci` followed by `echo test`) because its repeated `\S+\s+` tokens are not confined to one shell command. This violates the gate's central claim that a CI leg actually invokes the new package's test script.
issues.fix_hint: Parse individual `run:` command lines (including continuations as needed) and require the test command and package selector to belong to the same npm invocation; alternatively accept only a narrowly matched invocation with target working-directory. Add negative tests with multiple commands in one step, including root `npm test` plus a separate workspace-selected npm command, and `npm ci` followed by `echo test`.
issues.title: Unrelated commands in one workflow step can satisfy the package-test gate

verdict.summary: The new gate has a fail-open command-matching flaw: it searches an entire workflow step for an npm-test-shaped token sequence and independently searches that same step for a workspace selector. Consequently, unrelated commands in one step can be combined into a fictitious package test invocation, allowing a newly added package's tests to remain unexecuted. The tests cover selectors for the intended invocation but not separation between multiple commands, so they do not protect the load-bearing invariant.
